title: Diana, precision guide RNA design (iGEM UMA-Malaga 2026 software)
summary: Web app, F# library and CLI that turn disease variants into ranked CRISPR-Cas13 guide RNA spacers, flag restriction sites, export order-ready oligos and plan combinatorial guide pooling on 96/384-well plates. Official software deliverable of iGEM team UMA-Malaga 2026.
my_contribution: Sole developer, building the software for the team's scientists.
highlights: Built Diana as sole developer, a Blazor Server (.NET 9) app, F# library and CLI that convert disease variants (HGVS or rsID) into ranked CRISPR-Cas13 guide RNA spacers scored by GC content, homopolymers, Bowtie off-target alignments and ViennaRNA RNA folding.
Guide RNAs designed with Diana were ordered and tested in the wet lab by the iGEM UMA scientific team.
Implemented combinatorial guide pooling (2D fragmented, 2D matrix and 3D models) onto 96/384-well plates, decoding positive wells back to the implicated guides and flagging ambiguous collisions.
Added restriction-site flagging (BsaI, BsmBI, SapI, BbsI, EcoRI, PstI, XbaI, SpeI, EcoRV, NotI) and an order-ready oligo CSV export so designs go straight to synthesis.

Containerized Diana with a two-image Docker build that checksum-verifies and bakes in the GRCh38 index and runs as non-root with a health check, avoiding the more than 10x alignment slowdown of a mounted index.

title: Tokenized digital bond platform on Canton Network (UMA Blockchain Technologies × ioBuilders)
summary: Final project of the University of Málaga Blockchain Technologies course (run by NICS Lab; 18 students in 6 teams mentored by industry partners), built with ioBuilders. A Dockerized Canton network running a CIP-056 tokenized bond contract in Daml, a Go REST backend over the gRPC Ledger API, a web frontend to issue, transfer, burn and settle bonds with DvP allocations, a ledger event listener and a full observability stack.
my_contribution: Owned the Canton, blockchain and Daml layer, the system architecture, .NET Aspire orchestration and telemetry.
highlights: Designed the architecture and built the Canton/Daml layer of a tokenized bond platform on a local Canton network (sequencer, mediator, synchronizer, three participants) with a CIP-056 Daml contract and issue, transfer, burn and DvP settlement flows exposed through a Go REST backend over the gRPC Ledger API.
Orchestrated the platform with .NET Aspire and instrumented it with OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Tempo and Grafana; the bond lifecycle is covered by Playwright end-to-end tests.
Led to a Bachelor's thesis on Canton Network developed in collaboration with ioBuilders.

title: CUDECA WATT, donation and event platform (case study for Fundación Cudeca)
summary: Course project for "Análisis y Diseño de Aplicaciones" (University of Málaga) built on a real use case for Fundación Cudeca, a palliative-care charity. Donations with tax certificates, event ticketing with QR validation, memberships and an admin panel. Not a commercial or production system.
my_contribution: Responsible for the backend, CI/CD and architecture.
highlights: Owned the backend, CI/CD and architecture of CUDECA WATT, a full-stack donation and event platform built for a real charity use case (ASP.NET Core 9 Minimal API, Supabase, Stripe, QuestPDF tax certificates, QR tickets).
After months of requirements analysis and architecture design, the team completed the full implementation in 23 days under Scrum.

Set up GitHub Actions CI/CD that deployed every backend and frontend change automatically to Azure Web Apps from day one, and kept Swagger/Scalar API docs live so the frontend team never blocked on API changes.

title: DevOps & Cloud Course, 1st edition (ETSI Informática, University of Málaga)
summary: Four-week, four-session practical course for computer engineering students, co-organized and co-taught with Alejandro Cerezo Contreras. Covered containerization with Docker, Kubernetes orchestration, cloud deployment on AWS and Azure, GitHub Actions and platform engineering, with industry guest speakers (Docker Sevilla community organizer, a platform engineering module with Azure and Terraform, a Formula 1 digital-twin cloud case study). The final session was opened to the public with GitHub Community España.
my_contribution: Co-organizer and speaker (curriculum, sessions, guest speakers, course website).
highlights: Co-founded, organized and taught the first DevOps & Cloud course at the University of Málaga's School of Computer Engineering, a four-week program on Docker, Kubernetes, AWS/Azure deployment, GitHub Actions and platform engineering, bringing in industry guest speakers.

title: Aid-delivery verification on-chain, Blockchain For Good Hackathon 2026
summary: 24-hour hackathon organized by Cátedra Fintech and Fundación Kareema. Team of three built a donation-tracking system that detects, through an open BLE network, when a humanitarian aid package physically arrives and records the proof on-chain so donors can verify their impact. Javier was the team's blockchain lead; teammates had no prior blockchain background.
my_contribution: Blockchain lead; prepared an agent-ready EVM hackathon starter (Scaffold-ETH 2, Foundry, Next.js, CI/CD, gated deploys).
highlights: Built in 24 hours, with a team of three, a system that detects humanitarian aid package arrival over an open BLE network and records proof of delivery on-chain for donors; onboarded two teammates with no prior blockchain experience.
